absence_search_guard.leg_wide_limb: G23a ran over ALL 112 declared-unmatched rows in this run, with no exception list, and requires a non-empty `the_search_that_found_none` on each.
absence_search_guard.registry_limb_reach: G23b/c/d reach the rows carrying a `search_id`. The rows without one carry a PROSE search that was run and recorded but not registered in a re-runnable form; back-filling a registry entry for a search this run did not re-measure would be inventing the measurement, which is the defect the field exists to prevent. Stated as a bound, not papered over.
absence_search_guard.what_a_green_here_is_not: Evidence that any search was well-chosen. G23 checks that a search is NAMED, RUNNABLE and REACHED its population. Whether the population was the right one to look in, and whether the member's claim is really what the search looked for, are judgements — they are carried on the row in `why_this_search_is_this_claims_search` so a reader can disagree with them, and no refusal can reach them.

arithmetic.members_equation: population members = members with >=1 edge + members declared unmatched

axis_provenance.what_was_checked: every axis `expr`, every precondition `guard` and every listed conjunct occurs VERBATIM in the bytes at the span its row names — the emitting excerpt or a named context excerpt.

axis_span_provenance.what_this_does_not_establish: That a rejected row's span is the RIGHT one. It establishes that the row is not claiming the locator's authority for a span the locator did not give it. The bytes at the span are checked separately, and only when --harness is given.
axis_span_provenance.what_was_checked: For every `locator_row` row, the committed `emitting_byte_span` is one the locator names for that row's key. For every `locator_row_rejected` row, the locator's own `rung_pin_level` is NOT `row`, the span used is NOT one the locator names, and a reason is recorded. An unknown provenance value is refused.

citation_verbatim_guard.reach: `quotes_compared` equals `quotes_counted`, and that attests exactly one thing: NO QUOTE FAILED TO PLACE. It is NOT an independent recount, and by itself it is not evidence of reach. Both figures come out of ONE traversal in `audit/3` — `quotes_counted` is the length of the quote list that traversal built and `quotes_compared` counts the members of that same list which matched — so the equality is another spelling of `no quote-level defect`, and a sweep that read NOTHING satisfies it at 0 == 0, as does one reading a field that does not exist. What bears on reach here is the MAGNITUDE and never the equality: `quotes_compared` quotes placed, over `records_with_evidence` records, over `records_visited` visited. The independent recount — the span regex walked a SECOND time over the same records by code that is not `audit/3` — and the `counted > 0` that stops an empty population passing both live in `conformance/controls/citation_verbatim_controls.exs`, not in this artefact. The record population is every top-level list of objects in each edges file, so a collection a later ticket adds is inside the guard without being named here.
citation_verbatim_guard.what_it_does_not_establish: That a quote SUPPORTS the verdict it is filed under — that is a judgement and A3 §7's residual, and no refusal reaches it. That a backticked PROSE phrase is accurate: only source-shaped spans are compared, so an inaccurate paraphrase in backticks passes, and the ruling's remedy is to de-quote prose rather than to widen the shape test until English fails it. That a quoted byte-string in a field OTHER than `evidence` is verbatim — the gap between `records_visited` and `records_with_evidence` is exactly that population, reported rather than implied.
citation_verbatim_guard.what_was_checked: Every SOURCE-SHAPED backtick span in `evidence` — one carrying `=`, `(`, `[`, `!==` or `===` — occurs VERBATIM and CONTIGUOUS, modulo runs of whitespace, inside a window the evidence itself ADDRESSES: the cited `file.exs:N[-M]` span in the repo, or a byte span the axis row for this edge's tag names in the harness build. Two limbs: WINDOWING (the comparison is against the cited span, never the whole artefact) catches a right-bytes/wrong-line citation; CONTIGUITY (one squashed string, substring containment) catches a quote spliced from lines that are real and non-adjacent. A bare `:N` continuation is refused as a FORM — it has no syntactic referent and resolving it by proximity is guessing. An elision inside a source-shaped span is refused rather than fragment-matched, because matching `A … B`'s halves green-lights a quote whose parts sit arbitrarily far apart, which is the composed-quote hole this guard exists to close.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: The near miss, named — a zero with its near miss named is a search, a bare zero is a grep. The RUN CENSUSES carry `"reason": "extension"` on not_scored scenarios, and a reader meeting the word there could take it for a counterpart. It is not one: those are protocol-extension PACKAGING — scenarios outside the frozen set — and not SEP-2133 capability-extensions negotiation. MEASURED at this tip, on both censuses: 16 of the 20 not_scored entries carry that reason, 6 on the client leg (`auth/client-credentials-jwt`, `-basic`, `auth/enterprise-managed-authorization`, `auth/dpop`, `auth/dpop-nonce`, `auth/wif-jwt-bearer`) and 10 on the server leg (the `tasks-*` family). NOTE — cg-reconciliation.md §2 states this as "seven not_scored scenarios"; that figure does not hold and has not since it was written. The client leg has 7 not_scored ENTRIES, of which 6 carry `extension` — the 7th, `json-schema-2020-12-preservation`, carries `added-after-release`. Over both legs it is 16 of 20. The census has not changed since MES-57 (3e487f8), so this is not drift. The ZERO above is unaffected; the near-miss figure is what was wrong. Recorded here and reported as a finding against cg-reconciliation.md, which is change-controlled and is not edited from this ticket.
declared_unmatched.the_search_that_found_none: RUN AT THIS TIP BY C1b-ii, not quoted. `/extension/i` over the WHOLE row — scenario + check id + name + description — of all 175 manifest checks in docs/conformance/in-scope-2026-07-28.json returns 0. The sweep is shown to have REACHED that population rather than to have matched nothing for want of running: the same predicate over the same 175 rows returns 45 for `/header/i`, 36 for `/schema/i` and 8 for `/caching/i`. So the zero is a property of the population's content, not of the sweep. Corroborates cg-reconciliation.md §2's E0, which recorded the same zero from the CG side; this one is measured from inside the declared check population.
declared_unmatched.why_no_counterpart: `no-oc-scenario` — the suite has no such check ANYWHERE, so the search is over all 175 and not over a fixture. SEP-2133 extensions negotiation has no OC check on either leg: A4 §5 measured 0 of 175 and the search recorded above re-measures it here. This is CG2's whole shape and the reason it is a bucket-1 BLOCK rather than a correspondence question — there is nothing to correspond WITH.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `sep-2243-x-mcp-header-primitive-only` / `ClientRejectsInvalidTool_invalid_object_header` — `Client MUST NOT call tool 'invalid_object_header' with invalid x-mcp-header`. The word `object` is right there in a CG7 check, and it is not this case. Its fixture is `data:{type:`object`,"x-mcp-header":`Data`}`: an annotation whose OWN property is object-typed, which is invalid because only primitives may be mirrored. The claim here is the opposite and legitimate case — an annotation on a STRING property that sits inside another object's `properties` — and the reachability question (is every step of the chain a `properties` key?) is never put: the measurement above finds zero `properties:` nested inside a `properties:` anywhere in the two CG7 scenarios' 14027 bytes, while 14 `properties:{` and 55 `x-mcp-header` occurrences show the sweep reading the right bytes. Every annotation in the CG7 fixture sits one step down.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `sep-2243-client-encode-values` / `ClientCustomHeader_Priority` — `Client sends correct Mcp-Param-Priority header (INTEGER value)`. The suite does score an integer header value, on the client leg, in CG7, and this file already carries an edge to it. The value it scores is `42`. The safe-range boundary is 9007199254740991, sixteen digits; the search finds zero integer literals of sixteen digits or more in the two CG7 scenarios, and the largest integer anywhere in them is the 42 the positive control returns. So the constraint exists in the spec and in our implementation, the suite has a check in the right place, and its fixture never reaches the boundary.

declared_unmatched.the_search_that_found_none: Both CG7 scenarios' fixtures were read at the pinned build. `http-custom-headers` serves two tools and ONE argument vector — the 16 values of the alpha.11 `http-custom-headers` fixture's own argument vector, enumerated in header_mirror_test.exs:305-322 — and no value in it is sentinel-shaped (`=?base64?…?=`); `http-invalid-tool-headers` sends no annotated VALUES at all, only ten malformed tool DEFINITIONS (`Ua`). declared_unmatched.why_no_counterpart: streamable-http.mdx:508-510 requires a client to Base64-encode a plain-ASCII value that matches the sentinel pattern, or a server cannot tell an encoded value from a literal one. The scenario exists and is matched; its fixture holds no case that exercises the constraint — which is what `no-oc-fixture-case` names, as against `no-oc-scenario`.

declared_unmatched.the_search_that_found_none: All 29 CG7 checks were read. Each `ClientCustomHeader_*` check's predicate quantifies over ONE named header — `checkParamHeader` is called once per annotated parameter and `a=e.headers[i]` reads that parameter's header alone. No check's predicate quantifies over the header SET, and neither `ClientSupportsCustomHeaders` (`some(...)`, an existential over names, not values) nor the two NoMirror checks (`===void 0` on one named header) is universal either.
declared_unmatched.why_no_counterpart: The member asserts a UNIVERSAL property — no produced header value carries a raw CR or LF, and every produced header NAME is lower-case — over the whole 16-value vector. It is the injection-closure property, and it is stronger than the conjunction of the per-parameter checks: it would still fail if a SEVENTEENTH header appeared carrying a newline. Filing it on `ClientCustomHeader_CrLf` would report agreement on a check whose subject is one header's value.

declared_unmatched.the_search_that_found_none: RUN AT THIS TIP. The check-emitting code IS general over methods: `checkMcpMethodHeader` computes `ClientMcpMethodHeader_${n.replace(/\//g,`_`)}` from the body method, so a `notifications/cancelled` POST would emit `ClientMcpMethodHeader_notifications_cancelled`. No such key is in A1's 175 — no case in the scenario drives a notification, which is what `no-oc-fixture-case` names. The near miss is named rather than left for a reader to trip over: `/notification/i` over the whole row of all 175 returns 6, and exactly ONE is a routing-header check — `ClientMcpMethodHeader_notifications_initialized`. That one is OUT OF DENOMINATOR: A5's bucket-0 artefact records it `removed_by_spec` (`reason_code`), because 2026-07-28 removed the initialize handshake under SEP-2575, and it is one of the only 2 of 175 A5 excludes. So the nearest existing check is unavailable as a counterpart BY RULE, not by absence. The sweep is shown to have reached the population: `/response/i` over the same 175 rows returns 17.
declared_unmatched.why_no_counterpart: `no-oc-fixture-case` — the scenario exists and is matched, and its check-emitting predicate would score this behaviour; what is missing is a case that sends a notification. declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `ToolsCallError` (`Tool returns error correctly`, scenario `tools-call-error`) and `HttpServerErrorJsonrpcId` (`All error responses carry the request JSON-RPC id`, scenario `server-stateless`). Both are about a server REPORTING an error well, and a reader who greps for `error`, finds them and stops would take them for the counterpart. Neither is: `ToolsCallError` scores a TOOL's own declared failure being reported as a result, and `HttpServerErrorJsonrpcId` scores an envelope field. Neither asks what happens when the server's own per-request IDENTITY machinery fails — whether the request is contained at all, with what code, and whether the internal reason reaches the caller. That is an SDK-deployment obligation the suite has no vocabulary for: the conformance harness supplies no identity pipeline to break.

declared_unmatched.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: `ToolsCallEmbeddedResource` and `PromptsGetEmbeddedResource` — the suite's two other resource-bearing content checks, both declared here. They are NEAR MISSES and NOT counterparts, and the distinction is the protocol's own: an EmbeddedResource INLINES the resource contents in the result, while a ResourceLink is a REFERENCE the client must then read with `resources/read`. A check that finds an inlined resource would reject a link and vice versa. MEASURED WIDER THAN THE DECLARATION: the pattern is 0 over all 175 manifest rows and over both legs, not merely 0 over the declared 107, so this is not a deferral to another C1c slice — the suite has no ResourceLink check at all. That is a coverage finding about the OFFICIAL SUITE: `ResourceLink` is in the 2026-07-28 schema (its definition is at build bytes 293842-293989) and nothing in the conformance suite exercises it.

keying_control.measure: ROWS LOST — rows that disappear when the projection is deduplicated. A1's measure and match-relation.md §5's, so the keyings are compared in the unit those documents already use.
keying_control.the_row_this_leg_DEPENDS_on: `sep-2243-client-includes-standard-headers` — NINE in-denominator client checks share that one `check_id`: ClientMcpMethodHeader_tools_list / _tools_call / _resources_list / _resources_read / _prompts_list / _prompts_get and ClientMcpNameHeader_tools_call / _resources_read / _prompts_get, plus the 2 SKIPPED ones, 11 rows on one id. Keying on `check_id` would merge nine CLIENT checks into one; A1's six-field key merges none. It is CG1's whole scenario, so it is a row the client leg depends on rather than an example quoted from A1 — and it is why the control stays on the 173: re-scoped to CG7's 29, the `name` and `description` limbs lose NOTHING (measured 0 of 54 on the whole client leg) and could not fire at all, which is the vacuity the two-direction design exists to prevent.
keying_control.what_the_crosswalk_is_keyed_on: A3's token for the address and A1's six-field key for the join. The token carries five fields; `description` cannot live in a test name, so reversibility is THROUGH A1's manifest, not lexical.
keying_control.what_the_two_directions_establish: POSITIVE: the obvious keyings DO merge rows on this population, so the hazard is real here and not merely quoted from A1. NEGATIVE: A1's six-field key merges none. Either direction alone is vacuous — a control that only ran the second would pass over a crosswalk keyed on `id`.

checks_addressed_outside_the_declared_ch.what_this_is: Checks an edge addresses that no file declares. They carry adjudicated edges and take NO part in bucket 2, because bucket 2 is a complement and these checks are not in any declared universe to be complemented within.
checks_addressed_outside_the_declared_ch.why_this_is_not_refused: An edge addresses the check its claim is about; refusing one outside the declared check population would force a file to declare every scenario it touches, and then bucket 2 would report every UNADJUDICATED sibling as having no ET counterpart. That is the false claim the third state exists to prevent.

check_population.rule: EVERY in-denominator OC check on the CLIENT leg — all 54, across all seven of its scenarios. This file is total over them: every one is axis-decomposed, and every one either carries an edge or is reported in bucket 2 by name.

selector.denotes: All 54 in-denominator CLIENT checks — `http-custom-headers` 18 + `http-invalid-tool-headers` 11 (CG7) + `http-standard-headers` 9 (CG1) + `json-schema-ref-no-deref` 1 (CG4) + `request-metadata` 8 + `sep-2322-client-request-state` 5 + `tools_call` 2 (C1b-iii). Those seven scenarios ARE the client leg in the locator's artefact, so with C1b-iii's three added the declared check population and the client leg's in-denominator checks are the same set. The selector names the SCENARIOS rather than the 54 tokens, so a check added to any of them by a harness bump joins the population instead of falling silently outside it.
selector.evaluated: 54 checks denoted; equal to the count this file declares, and every one of them is axis-decomposed (G19).
selector.source_owner: MES-97 (C1a) — `mix conformance.locator`'s output, one row per in-denominator check
selector.what_this_is: The check half of the declaration, and the reason bucket 2 can now be non-empty. C1a derived its check population from the tags its own edges carried, so bucket 2 — the complement of the edge-bearing checks within it — was EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and its `CHECKED, AND ZERO` was a vacuous truth. Declaring the checks from outside the file is what makes the question answerable.
selector.why_the_locator_artefact_and_not_A1s_man: A1's manifest nests its checks under scenarios and its key is a six-field LIST; the selector's `key_field` must name a string field, and refuses anything else rather than stringifying it. The locator artefact is flat, carries one row per in-denominator check, and already carries the TOKEN — which is the field the edges in this file address checks by, so the two sides are compared in the same unit.

leg_totality.and_what_it_does_not: That any adjudication is RIGHT. It is a totality guard, not a correctness one: a leg every member of which was adjudicated wrongly passes it exactly as firmly. The state-4 guard over this population is still ENTAILED by G15a and still cannot fire (residual X7) — what G22b adds is that the population it cannot fire over is now provably the WHOLE leg rather than a slice somebody chose, and that scope claim is not entailed by anything.

files.rule: Every ET-CC member B2b attributes to the CLIENT leg. The leg is reached as the UNION of the four ticket slices that adjudicated it — CG7 (C1b-i), CG1/CG2/CG4 (C1b-ii), NO CG AT ALL (C1b-iii), and whatever C1a had already tagged — and the union is now the whole leg: every client row in B2b carries a `cg` in {CG7, CG1, CG2, CG4} or carries none, so the four limbs are exhaustive over it. NOTHING outside the client leg is adjudicated here.

selector.denotes: 107 ET-CC members — the WHOLE client leg. C1b-i declared 45 (CG7's 29 plus C1a's 18 moved rows, overlapping in 2). C1b-ii added 20 new homes from its 23 CG1/CG2/CG4 rows — three CG2 rows already sat inside the 45 through the `tokens` limb and were not re-homed — taking it to 65. C1b-iii's sub-population, `leg = client AND cg is_null`, is 55 rows and adds 42 new homes, not 55: THIRTEEN of the 55 carry C1a `oc:` tokens and so were already inside through the same `tokens` limb. 65 + 42 = 107. The one-home rule is preserved exactly by not re-homing those thirteen, which is the shape C1b-ii recorded for its three.
selector.evaluated: 107 members denoted; set-equal to the population this file derives in both directions (G15a). The counts block was checked field by field (G15b).
selector.is_null_is_not_get_equals_nil: The `cg is_null` limb is `has_key?(row, "cg") and get(row, "cg") == nil`. Under the weaker `get(row,"cg") == nil` an ABSENT field and a null one are the same thing, so a B2b schema change dropping `cg` would make the limb denote EVERY row and silently re-declare this population as all 281 — reconciling perfectly over a universe nobody chose. As implemented an absent field denotes NOTHING, the denotation collapses, and G15a reds naming every member as `extra`. Measured at this tip: all 281 rows carry the key, so the two readings are indistinguishable on live data and only a unit separates them. Both limbs are unit-tested and the absent-field case is shown separately (`crosswalk_controls.exs selectors`).
selector.what_this_is: The EXECUTABLE half of `rule`. The generator evaluates it against the source named below and requires the result to be SET-EQUAL, in both directions, to the population this file derives. Prose only becomes a guard when something can run it.
selector.why_it_must_name_a_file_other_than_this_: C1a derived its declared population by unioning the register_keys the edges file itself carried, so a dropped row did not violate the universe, it SHRANK it — measured on MES-99, both a dropped edge and a dropped declared_unmatched row built cleanly at 20 members with every set comparison still exact. A selector that read this file's own rows would be circular by another route.
selector.why_the_cg_conjunct_and_not_the_whole_cl: HISTORY, kept because the selector's SHAPE is a consequence of it. MES-104 was re-scoped to C1b-i = CG7 at the plan hop, so the leg arrived in three instalments — C1b-i CG7, C1b-ii CG1+CG2+CG4, C1b-iii the members with no CG — and the selector is the union of those slices. The union now covers the leg, and it is NOT collapsed into `leg equals client` for the reason recorded in `why_the_selector_is_still_a_union_of_slices_and_not_`leg_equals_client``.
selector.why_the_selector_is_still_a_union_of_sli: The four limbs now denote the whole leg, so `leg equals client` alone would denote the same 107 today — and it is NOT used, deliberately. G22b evaluates `all_of[{leg equals client}]` FRESH against B2b and set-compares it with this file's members. Under a bare-leg top-level selector that comparison would be ENTAILED by G15a's and could never fire: the X7 shape, a guard as empty as one nobody calls. Under the union shape the two ask different questions, and one mutation separates them — add a B2b row with `leg=client, cg="CG9"` and G15a stays green at 107 against 107 while G22b goes red at 108 against 107. That mutation is committed (`crosswalk_controls.exs totality`) and runs in the same run as the unmutated build.

check_population.rule: EVERY in-denominator OC check in the `server-stateless` scenario — all 30, C1c-i's — every in-denominator check in the FOURTEEN `input-required-result-*` scenarios — all 36, C1c-ii's: the MRTR family, SEP-2322's server side — AND every in-denominator check in the NINETEEN feature-endpoint scenarios, all 41, C1c-iii's: `tools-call-*` (7 scenarios) and `tools-list`, `prompts-*` (5), `resources-*` (4) and `sep-2164-resource-not-found`, and `completion-complete`. 30 + 36 + 41 = 107. This file is total over them: every one is axis-decomposed (12 by A3, 18 by C1c-i, 36 by C1c-ii, 41 by C1c-iii), and every one either carries an edge or is reported in bucket 2 by name.

selector.denotes: All 107 in-denominator checks of the thirty-four scenarios named: `server-stateless` 30, the fourteen `input-required-result-*` scenarios 36 between them, and the nineteen feature-endpoint scenarios 41 between them. THIRTY-FOUR clauses, where C1c-i had one and C1c-ii fifteen, and every one is an equality rather than a prefix — see `why_fourteen_clauses_and_not_a_prefix`, whose reasoning C1c-iii applies unchanged to `tools-`, `prompts-` and `resources-`.
selector.evaluated: 107 checks denoted; equal to the count this file declares, and every one of them is axis-decomposed (G19).
selector.source_owner: MES-97 (C1a) — `mix conformance.locator`'s output, one row per in-denominator check
selector.the_bound_this_leaves: The declared CHECK population is thirty-four scenarios of the suite's thirty-odd, so a bucket-1 row here means `no counterpart among these 107` and not `no counterpart anywhere` — `what_unmatched_means_in_a_file_that_declares_its_own_checks` in the client file states the rule and it is not restated. FOUR of this file's searches are scoped that way and say so in their `kind`: SRV02 and SRV18 name REAL counterparts in `dns-rebinding-protection` and SRV07 and SRV20 in `caching`, so that whichever later C1c slice declares those scenarios inherits the member instead of re-searching for it. C1c-i's SRV08 was a fifth, naming the `input-required-result-*` family; this ticket declared that family, so SRV08 is GONE and its member carries edges — the mechanism working, not failing.
selector.what_this_is: The check half of the declaration, and what makes bucket 2 answerable. It names the SCENARIO rather than the 107 tokens, so a check added to it by a harness bump joins the population instead of falling silently outside it.
selector.why_fourteen_clauses_and_not_a_prefix: A prefix clause would be SHORTER and would declare a DIFFERENT population: every future scenario whose name begins `input-required-result-` would join this file's declared checks the moment a harness bump introduced it, and would then have to be axis-decomposed by G19 or redden a build nobody had changed. Enumerating costs fourteen lines and makes the population a decision this ticket took rather than a pattern that keeps deciding. The same reasoning is why the client file enumerates its seven.
selector.why_the_feature_endpoint_scenarios_are_e: NINETEEN more equality clauses and not three `starts_with` ones. A prefix over `tools-` would be three lines instead of eight and would declare a DIFFERENT population: every future scenario a harness bump named `tools-call-something` would join this file's declared checks the moment it appeared, and would then have to be axis-decomposed by G19 or redden a build nobody had changed. The cost is real and is paid knowingly — the prefix would also have silently ADMITTED `tools-call-with-logging`, `tools-call-sampling` and `tools-call-elicitation`, three scenarios that exist in this very build and are NOT in this slice's 41. selector.the_four_modules_C1c_iii_adds_and_the_on: MES-116 (C1c-iii) adds FOUR module clauses and 16 members: the three content/type round-trip modules and the tool-ordering module. It DECLARES ALL 41 feature-endpoint checks and their whole 107-axis decomposition, but deliberately leaves ONE module of the feature-endpoint family undeclared — MCP.Server.JsonSchema202012Test, 31 members, 66% of the family's member load on its own. WHY THE SEAM IS BY MODULE AND NOT BY ENDPOINT, measured at dispatch and PM-ratified on 2026-09-23: the endpoint cut (`tools-*` against `prompts + resources + completion`) SPLITS ContentTest, whose five members are content-type round-trips that straddle it — TextContent, ImageContent, AudioContent and EmbeddedResource each reach both a `tools-call-*` check and a `prompts-get-*` one — and this file's partition needs every module declared exactly once. It also does not split the load: the endpoint cut puts 41 members on one side and 1 on the other. And it damages the decomposition, which G19 requires to be whole for every declared check: nineteen of the 41 checks are ONE generic validator at ONE span, so splitting the scenarios would split a single reading across two tickets for no gain. WHAT THE DEFERRAL COSTS, stated rather than assumed: nothing in this file has to be rewritten when the sibling lands. An undeclared member is `not_yet_adjudicated`, NOT bucket 1, so no absence search is owed for it, and bucket 2 is DERIVED by the generator rather than hand-listed. What the sibling can move is named in `the_bucket_2_entries_this_slice_records_as_provisional`.
selector.the_ninth_module_and_why_only_one_of_its: MES-115 (C1c-ii) adds ONE module, `MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTP.ACTest/`, and it is the whole of that ticket's member cut. MEASURED at 3166dc7: of the leg's 145 rows, exactly TWO carry a key that reaches the MRTR family at all — the stateless round-trip (already in this file, as SRV08's bucket-1 row) and ACTest's `spoof — MRTR retry with planted identity` — and ACTest is the only module holding one that was not already declared. Declaring the module is what makes an edge on that member POSSIBLE: G15a refuses an edge on a member outside the declared population, so the alternative was to leave the leg's second MRTR member to a slice that is not the MRTR ticket. The COST is stated rather than absorbed: the module's other four members (AC7 origin-403 parity, two AC8 identity-factory rows and the caching default) enter bucket 1 against checks that are not theirs, and each records a search and a `homed elsewhere` near miss so C1c-iv inherits them instead of re-searching — the SRV08 mechanism running the other way. PM-ratified on MES-115, 2026-09-23.

population_statement_guard: G21 — every population figure this generator's own prose states is one this run derived. Scanned 15 authored statements against the 23 distinct figures the run holds, and pinned 8 load-bearing phrases built from those figures independently of the text. THE UNIVERSE IS THE EMITTED ARTEFACT, not a list this module declares: a string is this generator's own iff it occurs in no input document, so a statement added later is inside the guard without anyone remembering to add it. This block is written AFTER the scan and is required to carry no population claim of its own, so it is not part of what it attests. BOUNDS: a figure spelled as a word, or stated without the noun it counts, is invisible to the scan — both occur here and are handled by interpolating them, not by the scan; a literal that coincides with some other held figure survives until the population next moves, which is when CR-5's recurrence would land anyway; and prose this generator does not EMIT (the moduledoc, a branch not taken) is outside the universe by construction.

residuals.text: THE CLIENT LEG IS CLOSED, BY REFUSAL AND NOT BY ASSERTION. Every ET-CC member B2b puts on the client leg carries a row here — all 107 of them — and a member in neither an edge nor a declared_unmatched record REFUSES THE BUILD (G22b), evaluated fresh against B2b and compared by set in both directions. The leg was reached by 4 ticket slices declared as a COVER and not a partition: 18 members sit in two slices at once, because a member a later ticket's CG brings in may already have carried an earlier ticket's token, and it keeps ONE home. The overlap is derived here, not taken from the file's word for it, so the slices cannot be summed into a leg that is not one. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a claim that any adjudication is right. A leg every member of which was adjudicated wrongly passes G22b exactly as firmly, and the state-4 guard over this population remains ENTAILED by G15a and unable to fire (X7) — what is new is that the population it cannot fire over is provably the whole leg rather than a slice somebody chose.
Axis verdicts are JUDGEMENTS. Whether a claim really agrees with a conjunct is A3 §7's semantic-sameness residual and escalates per case; nothing here decides it.

FALSIFICATION-TESTED by C3 (MES-99) and STANDING — the attempts were made and none succeeded, which is not the same as proven. The bound is narrow. The generator now refuses a duplicated join key (G14), a population that is not the set its external selector denotes or that disagrees with its own declared counts (G15), and a manifest whose verdicts have drifted from A5's bucket-0 artefact (G16). Every falsification class is shown firing on a mutated input with the unmutated build as the negative control in the same run, at the OS exit status and not only in-VM, and restored green after; C1a's own thirteen are re-run with the after-restoration they lacked. A per-row bucket-assignment drift is caught naming the row and the buckets it crosses (conformance/controls/crosswalk_falsification_controls.exs). What that does NOT establish: that any axis verdict is right (X1 is untouched — an axis verdict is a judgement and no refusal can reach it), and that anything outside the declared population was falsified at all. MES-104 added four refusals to the set C3 covers — G17 (two files declaring the same member), G18 (an axis row citing a provenance for its emitting span the locator does not support), G19 (a DECLARED check with no axis decomposition) and G20 (an inherited B2b token no row carries) — each shown firing on a mutated input with the unmutated build as the negative control in the same run. MES-108 added G21, which refuses a population figure in this generator's own prose that the run did not derive. What lies OUTSIDE the declared population is unfalsified, and the tickets that own it are the ones `population.outside_the_population.owners` names — this residual does not name them, because it named C1b-ii while C1b-ii was rendering it, and a statement that names its own producer as still owing the remainder is CR-1 (MES-104) recurring as CR-5 (MES-108).

The second-source re-derivation (`--verdicts-from bucket-0`) is a CONSISTENCY pin, not a correctness one (ruling 9). A1's manifest and A5's bucket-0 artefact are different files, different schemas, different generators — but both descend from the SAME accepted harness run. Byte-identical output witnesses that nobody edited one without regenerating the other. A wrong run would be wrong in both, and this pin would agree just as firmly.
Axis spans address ONE build. A harness bump invalidates them, and --harness is what detects it — a run without it records `harness_checked: false` rather than a pass.

`no_axis_contact` is a THIRD escalation, added here by generalising A3 §2's 'covering zero of one axis is no match, not a partial one' to N axes. A3 §3's table has no row for it. A3 §6's STATE-4 GUARD IS ENTAILED BY G15a and cannot fire. The population is set-equal to its selector's denotation in both directions and is derived from the file's own rows, so every member has a row and every row has a tag. This was already true in C1a, where the selector and the tagging predicate were literally the same predicate — so D3's claim that the state-4 guard 'is the limb that makes an EMPTY crosswalk fail' is not what happens: `check_population([], tagged)` returns `:ok`, and the vacuum guard is what fires. Recorded rather than removed, because the guard is A3 §6's ratified one and dropping it would be a silent change to a ratified rule. The completeness question that is NOT entailed is G20.

BUCKET 2 WAS EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION UNTIL MES-104. C1a derived its check universe from the tags its own edges carried, so the complement within it was necessarily empty and its `CHECKED, AND ZERO` could not have said anything else. A file may now declare its check population from an external anchor. This run's answer is 89 of the 161 declared checks carrying no edge from any ET-CC member. A file that declares none contributes none to the universe and the artefact reports that bucket 2 was not asked, rather than reporting a zero. The answer is interpolated — this sentence froze C1b-i's at nine and went on stating it after MES-108 moved the check population (CR-5).

A CLAIM-LEVEL STATE 3 HAS NO BUCKET. A3 §6's state 3 is a property of a MEMBER, and the bucket-1 reconciliation requires a member to be edge-bearing or declared unmatched, never both — so a member matching on some claims and not on others has nowhere to record the unmatched ones. C1b-i found five; MES-108 resolved two of them into real edges and found one more. This run carries 5 of them in `claim_level_unmatched`, each with the search that found none, and ESCALATED — the figure interpolated, because it was written as a word and so would not have moved (CR-5). Whether A3 §6 should gain a claim-level state is the PM's.

THE ABSENCE-SEARCH REGISTRY DOES NOT REACH EVERY BUCKET-1 ROW, and the shortfall is stated rather than hidden behind a green. G23's prose limb is LEG-WIDE with no exception list — every declared-unmatched row in this run records the search that found none, and the two rows that did not when MES-109 opened were fixed by RUNNING their searches, not by excepting them. verdict_mapping.rule: SUCCESS -> :green. FAILURE -> :red. WARNING -> :green carrying warning: true.
verdict_mapping.warning_basis: PM-ratified D2, measured not chosen: WARNING is leg-dependent — the client-leg reducer fails it, `requirements_exit` and the server-leg reducer ignore it — and BOTH in-denominator WARNING checks are on the server leg, where the reducer that would disagree does not apply.
verdict_mapping.warning_live_data: EXERCISED on 1 cell(s) of this run's population — the mapping fires on real data and is no longer unit-tested only. WHAT THAT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that it is RIGHT. A mapping that labelled every non-red check `warning` would fire here exactly as readily, so `exercised` and `correct` are different claims and only the first is made by this count. The second is the business of `conformance/controls/crosswalk_falsification_controls.exs warning_mapping`, which requires the real WARNING cell to land where the mapping sends it AND requires it to move OUT when the OC verdict is mutated away from WARNING.
verdict_mapping.warning_residual: A future CLIENT-leg WARNING needs its own ruling. The mapping must not be extended to cover one silently.
